en.name: Pâté
en.summary: Refrigerated pâté keeps 1–2 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 1–2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). It is a cooked, moist, low-acid ready-to-eat meat, and it is specifically named as a Listeria risk.
en.pantry: A chilled pâté is not a larder food, however traditional the crock looks. It is a cooked, moist, low-acid meat paste eaten without any further cooking, and refrigerated pâtés and meat spreads are specifically named among the foods that carry a Listeria risk — Listeria being the organism that grows even at fridge temperature. Out of the fridge give it two hours at most, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F). Serve a portion on a board and keep the rest cold rather than putting the whole terrine out.
en.fridge: 1–2 days from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. That is a short window and it is worth taking seriously: press cling film directly onto the cut surface so it does not oxidise and grey, keep it in the coldest part of the fridge rather than the door, and use a clean knife each time. Pregnant people are advised to choose pâtés and meat spreads sold in cans or that do not need refrigeration until opened, rather than the chilled kind — the shelf-stable versions are given as the safe substitute.
en.freezer: 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze it in its pot or in small ramekins with any fat layer intact, wrapped tightly, or cut a terrine into thick slabs rather than slices. Smooth liver pâtés can go slightly grainy on thawing as the fat separates; a coarser country-style one survives better. Any aspic or jelly does not survive freezing and will weep out. Freeze it early in the fridge window, not at the end of it.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight and use it within a day. Never thaw it on the counter, and do not refreeze.
spoilage: A sour, sharp or ammonia-like smell rather than a rich liver one.
A slimy or tacky film on the surface.
Grey-green discolouration beyond the normal darkening of a cut face.
Any mould, or fat that has separated and smells rancid.
tips: Press cling film onto the cut face; darkening there is oxidation, not spoilage.
Buy small amounts — the refrigerated window is very short.
Serve a portion and keep the rest in the fridge.
Pregnant people should choose canned or shelf-stable pâté instead.

faq.a: 1–2 days from purchase in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 1–2 months frozen at −18 °C.
Yes, 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze it in its pot with the fat layer intact; smooth pâtés can go slightly grainy.
Refrigerated pâtés and meat spreads are named as a Listeria risk and are on the avoid list. Canned or shelf-stable versions are given as the safe substitute.

zh.name: 法式肝醬（pâté）
zh.summary: 冷藏的肝醬自購買日起在 4 °C 以下可放 1～2 天，冷凍 −18 °C 下 1～2 個月。它是煮熟、含水、低酸性的即食肉品，而且被明確點名為李斯特菌的風險食品。
zh.pantry: 冷藏肝醬不是常溫食品，不管那個陶罐看起來多有傳統風味。它是煮熟、含水、低酸性的肉泥，而且不會再加熱就被吃掉；冷藏的肝醬與肉類抹醬被明確列在具李斯特菌風險的食品之中——而李斯特菌正是那種在冰箱溫度下仍會生長的細菌。離開冰箱最多兩小時，氣溫超過 32 °C 時最多一小時。請分一份到盤子上，其餘留在冰箱，而不是把整罐端出去。
zh.fridge: 自購買日起，4 °C 以下 1～2 天。這個期限很短，而且值得認真看待：把保鮮膜直接壓在切面上，避免氧化發灰；放在冰箱最冷的位置而不是門邊；每次都用乾淨的刀。針對孕婦的建議是選擇罐裝、或開封前不需要冷藏的肝醬與肉醬，而不是冷藏櫃裡的那一種——常溫版本被列為安全的替代選項。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 1～2 個月。請連同罐子或分裝到小烤皿冷凍，保留表面那層油脂，並確實包緊；整條肉凍則切成厚塊而不是薄片。細滑的肝醬解凍後可能因油脂分離而略帶顆粒感，粗顆粒的鄉村風反而撐得比較好。任何肉凍（aspic）都撐不過冷凍，解凍時會整個滲出來。請在冷藏期限的前段就冷凍，不要拖到最後。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍，並在一天內吃完。不要放室溫退冰，也不要二次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸、刺鼻或有氨味，而不是濃郁的肝香。
表面出現黏滑或發黏的薄膜。
出現超過切面正常變深程度的灰綠色。
長霉，或油脂分離並帶油耗味。
tips: 在切面壓上保鮮膜；切面變深是氧化，不是腐敗。
少量購買，冷藏期限真的很短。
分一份上桌，其餘留在冰箱。
孕婦請改選罐裝或常溫保存的肝醬。

faq.a: 自購買日起冷藏 4 °C 以下 1～2 天，或冷凍 −18 °C 下 1～2 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 1～2 個月。連罐冷凍並保留表面油脂；細滑的版本解凍後可能略帶顆粒。
冷藏的肝醬與肉醬被點名為李斯特菌風險食品，列在建議避免的清單上。罐裝或常溫版本則被列為安全的替代選擇。
